name: Celery
grown_as: Garden celery, a biennial grown as an annual for its fleshy leaf stalks. Trench celery is earthed up to blanch it; self-blanching varieties are paler and grown in blocks. ⚠️ CHECK which kind; drawn as green self-blanching celery. Celeriac (var. rapaceum) is the same species grown for its swollen base.
habit: First year an upright tight bunch of thick leaf stalks 40 to 60 cm tall with leaves at the top. If left, a second-year branched, grooved flowering stem 60 to 100 cm.

leaf.arrangement: A tight upright rosette from a short base
leaf.type: Compound, once pinnate, with 2 to 3 pairs of leaflets and an end leaflet
leaf.leaflets: Broadly wedge- to diamond-shaped, 2 to 6 cm, deeply three-lobed
leaf.outline: Oblong overall, carried at the top of the long stalk
leaf.base: Leaflets wedge-shaped, untoothed at the base
leaf.margin: Coarse blunt to sharp teeth on the outer edges of the lobes only
leaf.stalk: Long (20 to 35 cm), thick and fleshy, crescent-shaped in section, with strong ribs on the outer side and a groove on the inner; packed tightly together. Pale green to green.
leaf.colour: Mid green leaves on paler stalks

flower.form: Small flat umbels of tiny flowers
flower.carried: Often stalkless or short-stalked, opposite leaves and at the ends of branches, on 4 to 12 short rays
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: Tiny round-oval seeds 1.5 to 2 mm with fine pale ribs, brown when ripe
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves, then first true leaves three-lobed and toothed; slow to grow
winter: Nothing in most gardens: harvested by late autumn. Left plants can survive mild winters and flower the next year.

leaf: once pinnate with a few broad three-lobed leaflets
teeth on the outer edges only
bloom: small umbel of few short rays
young: upright stalks with divided leaves, the bunch starting to form
crop: tight upright bunch of thick ribbed pale stalks
flower: branched second-year stem with small greenish-white umbels close to the leaves
seedhead: small umbels of tiny brown seeds

look_alikes: Lovage is much taller, with a bigger glossier leaf and yellow-green umbels with bracts. Flat-leaved parsley has thin stalks and twice-divided leaves. Wild celery, the same species, has thin stalks.
